subject: OKR sync: customer health triage for upcoming QBR
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Execs <leadership@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: OKR sync: customer health triage for upcoming QBR

Team —

I'm pulling together the QBR packet for BrightWorks for next Wednesday and want to surface the health items that need exec attention and link these back to the relevant OKRs (primarily CS-OKR2 and Sales-OKR1). Please see the snapshot attached (health_snapshot_sep14.xlsx) and the short triage below.

High priority (need exec attention before QBR):
- BrightWorks (BW-459): Renewal risk increased to HIGH. Two issues: (1) performance variability on long-sequence generation over peak windows; (2) procurement requests for a custom SLA and data residency clause.
- Action requested: confirm whether we can offer a limited SLA addendum and prioritize a dedicated run of the 20k token stress test next Tuesday.

Medium priority:
- NovaRetail: onboarding delays due to evaluation dataset mismatch. Ownership: Tessa to lead prompt-set remediation.

Low priority:
- Several pilot accounts with minor latency spikes — ops ticket created and being monitored.

Specific asks for leadership before EOD Monday:
1) Vivek — approve escalation pathway for BrightWorks (commit to SLA negotiation window + possible credit).
2) Lauren — can legal draft a one-page SLA addendum and list non-negotiables we cannot accept? If yes, loop procurement.
3) Tessa — confirm readiness to run the extended stress test and estimated runtime.

Attached: health_snapshot_sep14.xlsx (summary + per-route token breakdown), SLA_tailoring_summary.pdf (one-pager drafts), mutual_action_plan_BW-459.docx (strawman MAP).

Thanks — I want to ensure the exec slide deck only contains items we have committed to or explicitly escalated.
— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Head, Customer Ops | Redwood Inference
---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Execs <leadership@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR sync: customer health triage for upcoming QBR

Thanks Aisha — quick read. Agree BrightWorks should be flagged. A few quick decisions from my side:

- Escalation path: approve a limited SLA addendum (up to 99.5% p95 uptime; credits capped at 10% ARR) pending legal sign-off. We should avoid open-ended financial exposure.
- Approve ops to run the extended stress test on Tue (priority slot). If the test confirms regressions, trigger contingency plan: fallback to smaller model variant + follow-up performance optimization sprint.
I'll need a clean bullet list for the exec slide with the exact ask phrasing (one sentence each). Aisha, can you convert the three action items into 1-sentence asks for the slide?
Vivek
VP, Commercial
---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Execs <leadership@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR sync: customer health triage for upcoming QBR

Aisha/Vivek —

We can draft a one-page SLA addendum. Quick legal guidance and constraints:
- We will not accept open-ended data residency guarantees beyond region-binding language (we can offer VPC + contract language referencing KMS controls, but on-prem/hard residency may require Private deployment contract).
- Credits: cap at 10% ARR is reasonable; require defined observable failure modes (p95 latency > X ms for Y minutes) rather than vague language.
- Change control: any model/quantization changes that materially alter performance must be communicated 30 days in advance and have a defined rollback path.

I'll prepare the one-pager and share a draft link by EOD. Also uploading a strawman MAP to the Drive (link below). For the exec slide: recommend the ask lines be: 

1) Approve limited SLA addendum (see one-pager) and credit cap at 10% ARR.
2) Authorize ops to run the 20k token stress test on Tue and commit to contingency fallback if regressions manifest.
3) Approve a PM-led remediation sprint if test fails (estimate 2 weeks).
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/0BwkB-Example/brightworks-qbr-pack
— Lauren
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: OKR sync: customer health triage for upcoming QBR

Hi Aisha / Vivek —

Thanks for the flag and for the draft approach. Quick clarifications from our side ahead of the QBR:
- We do need the SLA language to include a path for data residency certification for our EU customers — we understand Private deployment may be required, but we need clear gating criteria (what triggers escalation to Private).
- The procurement team would like a short timeline for remediation work and an estimate of how credits would be applied (examples help).

We can make the Tuesday stress test slot; please send the test window and any telemetry we'll be asked to provide.

Confirming: QBR proposed slot Wed 15 Sep 2027 09:00 PT. Please confirm and share the exec slide pack by Tuesday EOD.
Best,
Anna Li
Head of Platform Integration | BrightWorks
